pores.name: Pores
tips: Niacinamide helps regulate oil and refine the look of pores over time
A gentle BHA toner 2–3x/week keeps pores from clogging
Daily SPF slows the collagen loss that stretches pores

blackheads.name: Blackheads
tips: Double cleanse in the evening to fully remove sunscreen and oil
A BHA (salicylic acid) toner helps dissolve buildup inside pores
Avoid harsh scrubbing — it can irritate skin without actually clearing pores

texture.name: Texture
tips: A gentle AHA 1–2x/week smooths texture without over-stripping
Layering hydration (hyaluronic acid) plumps and softens rough patches
Consistency matters more than intensity — little and often beats occasional harsh treatments

oiliness.name: Oiliness
tips: Niacinamide helps regulate sebum without over-drying
Don't skip moisturizer — stripped skin often overproduces oil to compensate
A lightweight gel moisturizer keeps oil balanced without heaviness

dryness.name: Dryness
tips: Ceramides help rebuild the skin's natural moisture barrier
Layer hyaluronic acid on damp skin, then seal it in with a moisturizer
Cut back on strong actives (retinol, AHA/BHA) until the barrier recovers

redness.name: Redness
causes: Too many actives layered at once
tips: Centella asiatica (cica) is one of the most consistently soothing ingredients for visible redness
Simplify your routine temporarily while skin recalms
Patch-test new actives on your inner arm before applying to the face

sensitivity.name: Sensitivity
tips: Prioritize a ceramide-rich moisturizer to rebuild the barrier before reintroducing actives
Avoid layering multiple actives (retinol + AHA/BHA) until skin calms down
Look for fragrance-free formulas while your barrier recovers

spots.name: Dark spots
tips: Vitamin C in the morning helps fade spots and protects against new ones forming
Daily SPF is the single most effective way to stop spots from getting darker
Niacinamide can help even out tone alongside a brightening active

acne.name: Active blemishes
causes: Excess oil combined with clogged pores
tips: A BHA (salicylic acid) toner helps clear congestion inside the pore
Benzoyl peroxide spot-treats active, inflamed blemishes
Avoid picking — it prolongs healing and increases the odds of scarring

acneScars.name: Post-acne marks
causes: Slow cell turnover leaving marks visible longer
tips: Niacinamide and vitamin C both help fade lingering discoloration
Gentle, regular exfoliation (AHA) speeds up how fast marks fade
Consistent SPF prevents marks from darkening further in the sun

wrinkles.name: Fine lines & wrinkles
tips: Retinol is the best-studied ingredient for softening the look of fine lines over time
Peptides support skin firmness alongside retinol
Daily SPF is what actually slows new lines from forming

darkCircles.name: Under-eye circles
causes: Thin under-eye skin showing blood vessels
tips: A peptide eye cream can help with puffiness and the look of fine lines
Gently pat products in with your ring finger — never rub the eye area
Sleep and hydration have an outsized visible effect on this area specifically

radiance.name: Radiance
causes: Buildup of dull, dead skin cells
tips: Vitamin C brightens and adds visible glow with consistent use
Gentle exfoliation reveals fresher skin underneath
Radiance responds fast to hydration — don't skip your moisturizer step

faceScanPage.moduleDisclaimer: Use these suggestions as routine guidance. If the skin is painful, swollen or persistently irritated, ask a dermatologist.

pores: Cleanse gently at night so sunscreen and sebum do not sit in the pores.
Use SPF every morning; stretched-looking pores are worsened by sun damage.
Keep exfoliating acids to a planned rhythm instead of using them every day.
blackheads: Remove makeup and SPF fully before bed, then cleanse without scrubbing.
Use a BHA product gradually and pause if the skin feels tight or hot.
Avoid heavy layers on the nose and chin when the area is already congested.
texture: Keep a simple cleanse, moisturize and SPF base before adding strong actives.
Do not scrub texture; use chemical exfoliation slowly and consistently.
Sleep and stress matter here because irritation can make texture look rougher.
oiliness: Cleanse morning and evening, but avoid stripping foams that make skin rebound oily.
Use light layers and wait between products so the routine does not feel greasy.
Drink water through the day; dehydration can make skin feel oily and tight at once.
dryness: Apply moisturizer while the skin is slightly damp after cleansing.
Avoid hot water and long cleansing sessions that remove too much barrier lipid.
Layer hydration first, then seal it with a cream when the skin feels tight.
redness: Keep the routine short while the skin is reactive: cleanser, soothing serum, moisturizer, SPF.
Avoid stacking acids, retinoids and vitamin C on the same irritated evening.
Use lukewarm water and press products in gently instead of rubbing.
sensitivity: Patch test new products for several days before using them all over the face.
Introduce one new active at a time so reactions are easier to understand.
Prioritize barrier repair on recovery nights instead of chasing faster results.
spots: Use broad-spectrum SPF every morning and reapply when outdoors.
Pair brightening actives with patience; visible tone support takes consistent weeks.
Avoid picking marks because inflammation can deepen discoloration.
acne: Cleanse after sweat and remove sunscreen before sleep.
Keep acne actives targeted; more layers can irritate and worsen breakouts.
Change pillowcases often and avoid touching active breakouts during the day.
acneScars: Protect marks from sun every morning; UV keeps post-blemish color visible longer.
Use gentle resurfacing on a schedule, not on already irritated skin.
Do not pick healing blemishes; calm recovery reduces leftover marks.
wrinkles: Use SPF daily; UV exposure is the biggest routine-level factor you can control.
Keep retinoids mostly at night and alternate with recovery nights.
Moisturize consistently so dehydration lines are less visible.
darkCircles: Sleep consistency helps the under-eye area look less tired.
Use a tiny amount of eye product and avoid rubbing the area.
If puffiness is present, try a cool compress for a few minutes in the morning.
radiance: Cleanse at night so dull buildup does not stay under the next routine.
Hydrate before moisturizer; glow often drops when the skin is dehydrated.
Use SPF daily because pigmentation and dullness come back quickly with UV exposure.

retinol.name: Retinol / Retinoids
retinol.howToUse: Evening only, 2–3×/week to start, then build up as tolerated; always follow with SPF the next morning.
retinol.caution: Can cause dryness and peeling while skin adjusts. Avoid pairing with AHA/BHA or benzoyl peroxide the same night.

vitamin_c.name: Vitamin C (L-AA)
vitamin_c.howToUse: Morning, on clean skin, before moisturizer and SPF.
vitamin_c.caution: Can sting on very sensitive or broken skin — introduce slowly.

niacinamide.name: Niacinamide
niacinamide.summary: Regulates sebum, soothes, strengthens the barrier.
niacinamide.howToUse: Morning or evening; pairs well with almost every other active.
niacinamide.caution: Very well tolerated; only very high amounts occasionally cause flushing.

aha.name: AHA (glycolic / lactic)
aha.howToUse: Evening, 1–3×/week; rinse-off or leave-on depending on the product.
aha.caution: Increases sun sensitivity — daily SPF is essential. Don't combine with retinoids the same night.

bha.name: BHA (salicylic acid)
bha.howToUse: Evening or as directed, a few times a week; can be targeted on oily zones.
bha.caution: Introduce slowly to avoid dryness; patch-test if your skin is sensitive.

benzoyl_peroxide.name: Benzoyl peroxide
benzoyl_peroxide.howToUse: Once daily to start, as a short-contact or leave-on treatment on breakout-prone areas.
benzoyl_peroxide.caution: Can bleach fabrics and cause dryness. Avoid layering with retinol at the same time.

vitamin_e.name: Vitamin E
vitamin_e.summary: Antioxidant, often paired with vitamin C.
vitamin_e.howToUse: Morning or evening — usually already blended into serums and creams.
vitamin_e.caution: Rarely irritating; very high amounts can bother acne-prone skin.

peptides.name: Peptides / Copper peptides
peptides.howToUse: Morning or evening; play well with most other ingredients.
peptides.caution: Effects are gradual — consistency matters more than strength.

hyaluronic_acid.name: Hyaluronic acid
hyaluronic_acid.howToUse: Morning or evening on slightly damp skin, then seal with a moisturizer.
hyaluronic_acid.caution: In very dry air, always lock it in with a cream so it doesn't pull moisture from deeper skin.

centella.name: Centella asiatica (Cica)
centella.howToUse: Morning or evening; ideal for stressed or reactive skin.
centella.caution: Generally very gentle and well tolerated.

spf.name: Sunscreen (SPF)
spf.summary: UV protection — the final morning step.
benefits: Prevents UV damage and dark spots
spf.howToUse: Every morning as the last step; reapply through the day when outdoors.
spf.caution: The single most important step — actives like retinol and acids make daily SPF non-negotiable.

ceramides.name: Ceramides
ceramides.howToUse: Morning or evening, usually in moisturizers; layer over hydrating serums.
ceramides.caution: Very well tolerated — ideal for dry or compromised skin.

glass-skin.title: Glass skin
glass-skin.intro: Layered hydration and a barrier-friendly finish — light textures, no harsh actives fighting each other.
glass-skin.keepInMind: Glow comes from consistent hydration and daily SPF, not from stacking more actives.

acne-prone.title: Acne-prone
acne-prone.intro: Gentle cleansing, a pore-clearing BHA a few nights a week, niacinamide to calm, and spot treatment only where needed.
acne-prone.keepInMind: Don't use BHA and benzoyl peroxide plus retinol all at once — introduce one active at a time and give skin recovery nights.

anti-aging.title: Firmness & fine lines
anti-aging.intro: Antioxidant vitamin C in the morning, a retinoid a few evenings a week, peptides and rich moisture to support.
anti-aging.keepInMind: Retinoids need slow build-up and non-negotiable daytime SPF. Results are measured in months, not days.

brightening.title: Brightening & dark spots
brightening.intro: Vitamin C and niacinamide daily, a gentle AHA a couple of nights a week to renew the surface.
brightening.keepInMind: Sun exposure undoes brightening faster than any serum builds it — daily SPF is the real active here.

sensitive-barrier.title: Sensitive & barrier repair
sensitive-barrier.intro: Strip it back: gentle cleanse, soothing centella, humectants and ceramides to rebuild — no acids or retinoids while it settles.
sensitive-barrier.keepInMind: Fewer steps, fewer actives. Reintroduce anything strong only once skin feels calm and comfortable.

minimalist.title: Three-step minimalist
minimalist.intro: Cleanse, moisturise, protect. The smallest routine that still covers what actually matters.
minimalist.keepInMind: A simple routine you do every day beats an elaborate one you skip.

pregnancy-safe.title: Pregnancy-conscious
pregnancy-safe.intro: Focuses on ingredients commonly considered pregnancy-friendly — vitamin C, niacinamide, centella, hydration and SPF — and leaves out retinoids and salicylic acid.
pregnancy-safe.keepInMind: This is general information, not medical clearance. Always confirm any product with your doctor or midwife while pregnant or breastfeeding.

men.title: Men's essentials
men.intro: A short, effective routine — gentle cleanse, soothing centella (handy post-shave), niacinamide and daily SPF.
men.keepInMind: Shaving stresses the barrier; keep actives gentle and let irritated skin recover before adding anything strong.

teen.title: Teen skin
teen.goal: Gentle care for changing, breakout-prone skin
teen.intro: Keep it simple: gentle cleanse, a light BHA a couple of nights a week, niacinamide to calm, moisturiser and SPF.
teen.keepInMind: Don't over-strip — a stripped barrier makes breakouts worse. See a dermatologist for painful or persistent acne rather than stacking more actives.

winter.title: Winter barrier
winter.intro: Shift toward hydration and barrier support — humectants, ceramides and an optional facial oil to seal, with cleansing kept gentle.
winter.keepInMind: In dry indoor air, always seal humectants with a cream or oil. Ease off strong actives if skin feels tight or flaky.

summer.title: Summer lightweight
summer.intro: Antioxidant vitamin C in the morning, niacinamide for oil balance, a light emulsion, and diligent SPF.
summer.keepInMind: Reapply sunscreen through the day. Antioxidants support protection but never replace SPF.

exposure.title: Active ingredient exposure
exposure.subtitle: An overview of the actives your routine repeats or stacks.
exposure.redundant: You use {ingredient} across {count} products. That's not necessarily a problem, but the repetition probably doesn't give {count}× the benefit.
exposure.irritantStackEvening: Your evening routine stacks several potentially irritating actives ({ingredients}). Consider spreading them across different evenings rather than the same night.
exposure.irritantStackMorning: Your morning routine stacks several potentially irritating actives ({ingredients}). Consider spreading them out rather than layering them together.
exposure.concentrationNote: Haru reasons about which actives are present and how often, not their dose — concentrations aren't disclosed and are never guessed from a product's place in the INCI list.

weeklyRhythm.title: Weekly rhythm
weeklyRhythm.subtitle: A suggested evening cadence that spaces out your strongest actives.
weeklyRhythm.amNote: Your morning stays the same every day: gentle cleanse, hydrate, moisturiser, and SPF.
weeklyRhythm.noStrong: Your routine has no strong actives (retinoids, AHA/BHA) that need spacing out — a simple, consistent evening routine works well.
weeklyRhythm.disclaimer: A suggested rhythm, not a prescription — adjust to your own tolerance, and skip an active whenever your skin feels irritated.

reactions.title: Reaction journal
reactions.subtitle: Log how your skin felt after use — Haru looks for patterns over time.
reactions.recurrenceNote: A personal pattern, not medical proof the product caused it. If a reaction is strong or persistent, pause the product and consider a professional.

protocol.title: Routine Lab
protocol.subtitle: Change one thing, watch what happens, then decide — no ten changes at once.
protocol.principle: Keep everything else the same — changing one thing at a time is the whole point, so you can tell what actually works.
protocol.disclaimer: Haru describes likely contributors, not proof that one product caused a change. Stop any active if your skin becomes irritated.
protocol.evidenceStats: {notes} notes · {days} documented days · {missing} days without notes
protocol.evidenceNote: Days are counted in UTC. Missing notes do not mean no reaction or confirmed product use. This summary does not establish causation.

report.title: Skin summary
report.intro: A summary of your Haru profile, latest scan, routine and logged reactions to share with a dermatologist or other professional. It's a consumer cosmetic tool — not a diagnosis. If a concern is painful, persistent or worsening, please see a professional.
report.noScan: No face scan on record yet.
report.disclaimer: Scores are visual cosmetic estimates from ordinary photos, not clinical measurements, and Haru describes likely contributors rather than causes. This summary does not replace an in-person assessment.
report.entryText: Export your profile, scan and reactions as a summary to bring to a dermatologist.
report.auditLive: Live calculation from the current routine
report.redundantFinding: {ingredient} appears in {count} products. Keep one main source so tolerance is easier to read.
report.stackFinding: {slot}: strong actives are stacked ({ingredients}). Separate them or add recovery nights.
report.hydrationAdvice: Drink regularly through the day; dehydration can make skin look dull, tight and oily at the same time.
report.sleepAdvice: Keep the evening routine simple when sleep is short; the barrier tolerates fewer experiments on tired nights.
report.stressAdvice: If stress is high, avoid adding several active products at once; watch redness, picking and stinging.
report.sunAdvice: SPF is the condition for safe brightening, retinoid and exfoliation work; reapply outdoors and after sweat.
report.sportAdvice: After sport, cleanse sweat gently and avoid strong acids immediately if the skin feels hot or red.
report.sweatAdvice: Sweat plus sunscreen can clog easily; evening cleansing matters more on active days.
report.recoveryAdvice: Use recovery nights after intense workouts, poor sleep or visible irritation: cleanser, moisturizer, no extra active.

advice.uvHigh: High UV today — make SPF the priority and reapply through the day.
advice.humidHigh: Humid today — keep the morning routine light so it doesn't feel heavy.

advice.cold: Cold and indoor heating — expect drier skin and support the barrier.

retinol_aha_bha.headline: High over-exfoliation risk
retinol_aha_bha.reason: Retinol and AHAs both speed up cell turnover: combined the same night, they multiply redness, sensitivity and peeling.
retinol_aha_bha.recommendation: Alternate nights (e.g. retinol Mon/Wed/Fri, AHA the other nights) instead of layering them.

retinol_bha.headline: High over-exfoliation risk
retinol_bha.reason: Same logic as with AHAs: BHA and retinol stack irritation on an already fragile skin barrier.
retinol_bha.recommendation: Give each its own evening, never both at once.

retinol_benzoyl.headline: Benzoyl peroxide deactivates retinol
retinol_benzoyl.reason: Benzoyl peroxide oxidizes retinol and significantly reduces its efficacy, on top of irritating skin if combined.
retinol_benzoyl.recommendation: Use benzoyl peroxide in the morning and keep retinol for the evening, spaced by a few hours — or alternate days.

vitc_retinol_timing.headline: Two powerful actives, two different moments
vitc_retinol_timing.reason: L-AA vitamin C is unstable at a pH close to active retinol; combining them can neutralize part of their efficacy and irritate skin.
vitc_retinol_timing.recommendation: Vitamin C in the morning (antioxidant + protection), retinol at night. Simple, effective, zero conflict.

aha_bha_together.headline: Stacking exfoliants
aha_bha_together.reason: Using two chemical exfoliants the same evening raises the risk of a damaged skin barrier, especially on sensitive skin.
aha_bha_together.recommendation: Pick one per evening, or reserve the combo for very tolerant skin starting at low frequency.

niacinamide_vitc_myth.headline: Myth: this combination is actually safe
niacinamide_vitc_myth.reason: The belief that niacinamide + vitamin C form an ineffective complex comes from old studies at very high temperatures, not representative of a real routine.
niacinamide_vitc_myth.recommendation: You can use them together without issue. If your skin reacts, this combination isn't the cause — look at concentration instead.

peptides_aha.headline: Acidic pH can deactivate some peptides
peptides_aha.reason: Many peptides work best at neutral pH; an acidic exfoliant applied right before can reduce their efficacy.
peptides_aha.recommendation: Apply peptides at another time (morning routine, or a layer after rinsing/neutralizing the pH).

spf_am_only.headline: Retinol increases photosensitivity
spf_am_only.reason: Retinol makes skin more sensitive to UV. Since it's an evening product, the real thing to manage is your SPF the next morning.
spf_am_only.recommendation: No same-evening application to manage — just make sure to apply SPF the morning after a retinol night.

reliability.title: Haru reliability engine
reliability.subtitle: The routine is not a generic list: Haru combines photo quality, your saved products, ingredient exposure, reactions, weekly rhythm and environment before giving guidance.
reliability.scanText: Poor lighting, blur, face angle, filters and covered zones are flagged so Haru avoids pretending to see what it cannot see.
reliability.passportText: Each scan is saved as a comparable checkpoint with confidence per zone, so progress is read cautiously over time.
reliability.exposureText: Repeated actives, AM/PM placement and strong-active stacking are checked across the whole routine.
reliability.protocolText: One change at a time, with 7/14/28-day checkpoints, so cause and effect stay readable.
reliability.reactionsText: Recurring discomfort can be linked back to a product or routine change instead of being lost in memory.
reliability.environmentText: UV, humidity, dryness, cold and air quality can adjust the daily guidance without changing the whole routine.
reliability.reportText: The export separates what Haru knows, what is uncertain, and what should be watched or checked professionally.
reliability.passportIntro: A clear snapshot of your latest face scan, local conditions and reliability signals before Haru reads the routine.
reliability.noSkinProfile: No skin profile yet. Run the skin type exercise to complete this passport.

analysisAdvice.title: Priorities to complete the routine
analysisAdvice.subtitle: Haru found a few missing basics before the routine can be read reliably.
analysisAdvice.completeText: Cleanse, moisturize, protect and AM/PM placement are covered. Next, focus on rhythm, duplicated actives and how your skin reacts over time.

cleanser.title: Add a gentle cleanser
cleanser.text: A routine audit needs a clear cleansing step, especially at night, so sunscreen and makeup do not stay on the skin.

moisturizer.title: Add barrier support
moisturizer.text: A moisturizer or barrier cream helps Haru balance strong actives and prevent a routine from becoming too stripping.

spf.title: Add daily SPF
spf.text: Without sunscreen in the morning routine, brightening, retinoids and exfoliation are harder to judge safely.

morning.title: Build the morning side
morning.text: Morning should focus on protection: light hydration, antioxidant support if tolerated, and SPF.

evening.title: Build the evening side
evening.text: Evening should focus on removal and recovery, with stronger actives placed slowly and not all on the same night.

goodHabits.title: Start with skin logic, then personalize.
goodHabits.subtitle: Haru does not pretend everyone needs the same routine. The base is simple: cleanse, treat carefully, moisturize, protect. Then the details change by skin type.
goodHabits.rulesTitle: Rules Haru uses when checking a routine
goodHabits.disclaimer: Based on dermatologist-style routine basics: gentle cleansing, moisturizing, broad-spectrum SPF 30+, cautious active use, and sunscreen reapplication outdoors. Haru is guidance, not a medical diagnosis.

daily.title: Morning is protection
daily.text: Cleanse only if you wake up oily or sweaty, hydrate, then finish with broad-spectrum SPF 30 or higher every day.

daily.title: Evening is removal and repair
daily.text: Remove sunscreen and makeup, cleanse gently, then use treatment only if your skin tolerates it. Finish with moisturizer.

daily.title: SPF is the non-negotiable step
daily.text: Reapply about every 2 hours when outdoors, and after sweating or swimming. Actives work better when UV is controlled.

daily.title: Do less when skin is irritated
daily.text: Pause retinoids, acids, scrubs and fragrance-heavy extras when skin stings, flakes, burns, or stays red.

routines.am: Gentle rinse or creamy cleanser -> hydrating toner/serum -> ceramide moisturizer -> SPF.
routines.pm: Cleanser -> hydrating serum on damp skin -> richer moisturizer or sleeping mask.
routines.avoid: Avoid foaming cleansers that leave skin squeaky, daily acids, and layering too many actives.

routines.am: Light cleanser -> niacinamide or calming serum -> gel moisturizer -> lightweight SPF.
routines.pm: Cleanser -> BHA 2-4 nights/week or acne treatment -> non-comedogenic moisturizer.
routines.avoid: Do not skip moisturizer; over-stripping often makes oiliness worse.

routines.am: Minimal cleanse -> centella/panthenol serum -> barrier cream -> mineral or gentle SPF.
routines.pm: Cleanser -> soothing serum -> ceramide moisturizer. Add actives one at a time only.
routines.avoid: Avoid starting retinol, vitamin C and exfoliating acids in the same week.

routines.am: Gentle cleanser where needed -> light hydration -> moisturizer only where dry -> SPF.
routines.pm: Cleanser -> treatment by zone: BHA on oily areas, barrier care on dry areas -> moisturizer.
routines.avoid: Do not force one heavy routine on the whole face if your T-zone and cheeks behave differently.

routines.am: Cleanser -> vitamin C or niacinamide -> moisturizer -> SPF.
routines.pm: Cleanser -> gentle AHA 1-3 nights/week or retinoid on alternate nights -> moisturizer.
routines.avoid: Do not exfoliate daily for glow. Irritation creates more uneven tone.
Add only one new product at a time, then wait 1-2 weeks before adding another active.

rules: Apply thinnest textures before thicker creams.
Keep retinoids mostly at night and pair them with morning SPF.
Use exfoliating acids gradually; more tingle is not more result.
Patch test new actives, especially if your skin is reactive.
A routine that you can repeat beats a 12-step routine you abandon.
